Lesson 5 · Technical continuation

How should we compare different stores?

The same stores, calculation, and decision—with the specification and reproducible steps visible.

Baseline profiles · weeks 1–8 · the same 150 stores

← Return to the worked analysis

Read here or present the same material, one step at a time.

Use the same analysis rows

Fit the same 150 store-level baseline profiles as Lesson 4. Design columns are [1, lead, urban, demand−100, promotion_share, lead×urban]. There are no treatment indicators because the baseline precedes all alert policies.

Case seed: 20261109. All ten labs use the same store IDs and underlying records. Read the shared data dictionary.

Reproduce the calculation

A scenario row x yields prediction xβ. The lead slope is b1+b5×urban. A contrast between two specified profiles is (xA−xB)β; keeping the full row visible prevents an interaction from being omitted accidentally.

s = world()['stores']
X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(s)),s.lead_days,s.urban,s.baseline_demand-100,s.promotion_share,s.lead_days*s.urban])
beta = np.linalg.lstsq(X, s.baseline_rate, rcond=None)[0]
rural_slope = beta[1]
urban_slope = beta[1] + beta[5]
assert np.isclose(urban_slope, lesson_result(5)['urban_slope'])

# Verify the omitted-variable identity on a fixed sample.
stores = world()['stores']
x = stores.lead_days.to_numpy()
y = stores.baseline_rate.to_numpy()
short_X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(x)), x])
long_X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(x)), x, stores.urban])
short, _, _ = fit_ols(short_X, y)
long, _, _ = fit_ols(long_X, y)
sorting, _, _ = fit_ols(short_X, stores.urban)
assert np.isclose(short[1], long[1]+long[2]*sorting[1])

The code runs after the shared setup in the notebook. The downloadable script includes that setup and runs on its own.

Read the model and uncertainty

The displayed RMSE is in-sample fit on store-average baseline rates. Changing the input set changes the comparison; it does not by itself identify the causal effect of altering delivery time.

Change one analytical choice

Construct two profiles for a store team’s actual demand and promotion plan. Change only the characteristic under discussion and explain which fitted contrast you have calculated.

Matrix notation and interval targets

β̂ = (XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀy, when X has full column rank

The implementation uses a least-squares solver rather than explicitly inverting XᵀX. HC1 robust covariance rescales the sandwich covariance by n/(n−k). A fitted mean at row x₀ has estimated variance x₀ᵀVar(β̂)x₀. A classical individual prediction interval additionally includes residual variance and assumes an appropriate model for that future variation.

OVB identity: β short − β long = γ omitted × δ sorting

The identity is verified for the lead-only model, the lead-plus-location model, and the auxiliary location-on-lead regression. The broader six-column model then adds demand, promotions, and an interaction. The different specifications have different interpretation targets; their coefficients should not be compared without naming the held-fixed variables.

How this case is generated

The shared world contains 150 stores followed for 32 weeks. Delivery time, location, demand, promotions, store differences, and a common time pattern generate the probability of a stockout. Each store-week contains 140 product-days. The generator draws their availability and records both policy paths using the same underlying draws.

The expected alert reduction varies with delivery time and location. Offers are randomized only within the 50-store pilot cohort. Voluntary adoption uses measured starting conditions in a separate cohort. The final cohort starts a selected rollout in week 25. These are distinct studies inside the same business history.

Inspect the numerical mechanism

p0 = 0.055 + 0.014 × lead + 0.0005 × (demand − 100) + 0.018 × urban + 0.003 × (lead − 3) × urban + 0.020 × promotion + store effect + 0.006 × sin(week / 4)

Expected reduction = 0.006 + 0.008 × lead + 0.004 × urban; p1 = p0 − reduction

The probabilities are converted to counts by comparing 140 uniform draws with p0 or p1. Cost is 6 CU per stockout product-day plus 20 CU per week when alerts are offered. These costs are the stated management accounting scenario. The complete assignment rules, random streams, and calculations are in the shared source.

Read the shared generator and analysis source

Compare with the known answer

The shared baseline mechanism contains an interaction between delivery time and urban location. The fitted profiles recover an estimate of that pattern from the same store records used for the simple regression.
